newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank results meet top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank results meet top forecasts.

text.p: Bank of Beirut's 72.5 percent rise in mid-year profits met top market expectations and will support a further rise by the share on the Beirut Stock Exchange, brokers said on Thursday.
BOB announced a 72.53 percent increase in profits to $4,096,200 in the first half of 1997 from $2,374,000 in the first half of 1996 and $1,593,000 in the first quarter of 1997.
"The results are in line with the top expectations of $8 million profits for the year," a broker, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

Nicholas Sawan, head of trading at Beirut Finance House Lebanon Invest, said BOB had been expected to make $7 million in net income for 1997. "So, the results are higher than expectations. That's not bad at all".
He said the share price was expected to appreciate further. "There is still room for the share to rise".
"The results look quite good, very aggressive in fact. The P/E ratio is calculated at 12.82 which is quite reasonable," said a third broker.
Since listing on the Beirut Stock Exchange on April 11, BOB's share price has more than doubled to $4.375 from $2.17.
The share touched $4 on June 4 but then fluctuated below that level until June 27 when it began rising.

"Two weeks ago there was great resistance at the $4 level. The share broke this resistance due to a general feeling that the bank was going to make about $4 million in profit in the first half of 1997," a broker said.
"A rise in the share price up to $4.5 would be discounted, I would say," he added.
BOB ranked 13th among Lebanon's 82 banks in terms of profits in 1996, according to Bank Data Financial Services.

"Bank shares are expensive in Lebanon but since banks are growing tremendously, people are accepting to pay high premiums on the shares. As long as banks keep this growth momentum, the trend should continue moving upwards," a financier said.
